declared.title: From Thought to Action: Effects of Process-Versus Outcome-Based Mental Simulations on Performance
declared.foundIn: scout notes on Manson's ideas (idea 3); Crossref search « Pham Taylor from thought to action process versus outcome based mental simulations » (2026-11-23)

population: first-year college students before a midterm exam (US): process, outcome, both, or self-monitoring control for 5 to 7 days

findings.text: Rehearsing the steps of studying for 5 to 7 days before an exam increased studying and improved grades, through better planning and less anxiety

support.sentence: Results indicated that process simulation enhanced studying and improved grades; the latter effect was mediated by enhanced planning and reduced anxiety.

limits: a single study of first-year students at one university
Cole 2021 (full text) codes its grade effect against the control group as not significant (p < .09)
the abstract does not say how outcome simulation compared with the control group
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa
